references.text: The brothers elaborate on their claim and say they are twelve brothers, sons of one man in the land of Canaan, that the youngest is with his father, and that one is no longer present.
The brothers tell Jacob that they said to Joseph they were honest men and not spies, and that they are twelve brothers, sons of one father.
The brothers explain to Jacob that the man (Joseph) asked detailed questions about their family and lineage, which relates to their explanation of shared origin.
Judah explains the family background to Joseph and mentions their father and youngest brother, strengthening the claim that they are sons of one man and not spies.
Direct continuation of the same dialogue in the same event; confirms the brothers' ongoing defense of their honesty.
Direct response in the same dialogue; shows how Joseph's demand (to bring Benjamin) tests the truth of the brothers' claim to be 'honest people'.
